claim.measures: which operations each named identity was OBSERVED to reach, using the specimen values supplied by the operator
claim.does_not_measure: whether any observed access is authorized, and how many objects a reached operation exposes
claim.statement: The access matrix records observed responses. Reach is an observation, not a verdict: an operation an identity reached may be exactly what policy intends. Blast radius is a lower bound on observed reach, not a measure of exposure. Anomaly candidates are inconsistencies in the observations; they are hypotheses to declare and test, never findings.

limitation: Blast radius is measured at OPERATION level. It reports which endpoints an identity was observed to reach using the specimen values you supplied. It does not report how many objects those endpoints expose. Veridor probed at most 1 specimen(s) per operation and never enumerated identifiers. An operation counted as reached may expose one record or every record.

safety.posture: The access matrix issues one request per operation per identity per specimen. That is categorically closer to scanning than to testing. Use it only against systems you own or are explicitly authorised to test.
